Speaker: Nora
Line: I finally signed the lease for the bakery on Mulberry Street.

Speaker: Iris
Line: The one with the green awning? It’s adorable.

Speaker: Nora
Line: The wood-fired oven alone cost more than my car.

Speaker: Theo
Line: - Is the oven gas? - No, it's wood-fired, like I said.

Speaker: NORA
Line: We open Saturday at seven, sourdough and cinnamon knots.

Speaker: Iris
Line: l think you're brave. Or broke.

Speaker: Nora
Line: The starter is named “Gerald” and he is eleven years old.

Speaker: Theo
Line: You named the yeast?

Speaker: Nora
Line: Gerald has outlived every one of my relationships.

Speaker: Iris
Line: That's… actually sweet.

Speaker: Maya
Line: Save me a loaf. I'll bring the coffee.

Speaker: Maya
Line: Later that night, the bakery smelled like burnt caramel.

Speaker: Nora
Line: The first batch is ruined.It went completely black.

Speaker: Iris
Line: Burnt?

Speaker: Nora
Line: Carbonized. Gerald is disappointed in me.

Speaker: Theo
Line: - Start again. You still have until Saturday.

Speaker: Nora
Line: Fine. But nobody tells the customers about batch one.

Speaker: Maya
Line: Your secret dies with the cinnamon knots.
The oven door creaked open again at midnight.

Speaker: Nora
Line: Batch two. Gerald, don't let me down.

Speaker: Iris
Line: Has anyone seen a grey greyhound named Pickle?

Speaker: Sam
Line: He slipped his collar near the fountain in the park.

Speaker: Iris
Line: You lost my dog?

Speaker: Sam
Line: Technically, he lost himself. Greyhounds are fast.

Speaker: Maya
Line: We'll make posters. Big ones, with his good side.

Speaker: Iris
Line: Pickle doesn't have a bad side.

Speaker: Mr. Price
Line: I printed two hundred posters at the copy shop.

Speaker: Theo
Line: Two hundred? The whole neighbourhood will know his name.

Speaker: Iris and Maya
Line: That's the point!

Speaker: Nora
Line: Wait. Have you checked the bakery?

Speaker: Iris
Line: Why would a greyhound be at the bakery?

Speaker: Nora
Line: Because somebody keeps stealing the cinnamon knots.

Speaker: Sam
Line: I'm going to the bakery right now.

Speaker: Nora
Line: He was asleep under the counter the whole time, next to the flour sacks.

Speaker: Iris
Line: Pickle, you thief.

Speaker: Mr. Price
Line: I suppose I should recycle the posters.

Speaker: Maya
Line: The gallery wants twelve watercolors by the first of March.

Speaker: Theo
Line: Twelve? You've painted four.

Speaker: Maya
Line: Four good ones. The cobalt blue harbor is the best.

Speaker: Sam
Line: I'm Sam, the gallery assistant. We need the titles by Friday.

Speaker: theo
Line: Call the harbor one 'Low Tide in Cobalt'.

Speaker: Maya
Line: That's terrible. I love it.

Speaker: Iris
Line: What happened to the one with the lighthouse?

Speaker: Maya
Line: I spilled espresso on it and called it experimental.

Speaker: THEO
Line: Experimental sells. Ask any curator.

Speaker: Sam
Line: The curator asked for more lighthouses, actually.

Speaker: Maya
Line: Then the espresso stays.

Speaker: Nora
Line: I'll cater the opening. Mini croissants.

Speaker: Maya
Line: Only if Gerald behaves.

Speaker: Theo
Line: The following week, the watercolors sold in one evening.

Speaker: Maya
Line: Eleven sold. The espresso one went first.

column1: ('Theo', 'Right on time. The rooftop is ready.')
('Iris', 'Paper lanterns everywhere. It looks like a festival.')
('Nora', "I brought forty cinnamon knots and Gerald's apology loaf.")
('Theo', "It's a thunderstorm in exactly ten minutes, according to my phone.")
('Iris', 'Then we move the party to the stairwell.')
('Nora', 'The lanterns are melting in the rain.')
('Maya', 'Leave them. It looks like a painting.')
('Theo', 'Best party of the year, and nobody got struck by lightning.')
